setup_summary.text: The next report (fiscal Q4 2026) is expected 2027-01-19 after the close, and no confirmed date exists yet. Consensus is EPS $1.42 and revenue $8.16B. Whisper EPS, options-implied move and beat/miss record were not available. The average closing move over the last 8 reports is ±1.9%.

Q3 2026 (reported Oct 15) was a record quarter. Revenue was about $8B (+8.7% y/y) and diluted EPS $1.34 (about +10% y/y, or +16% excluding a reserve build worth about $0.07). Reported expenses rose 7.1% (2.0% ex-BTIG), NIM was 2.84% (+5bp q/q), net charge-offs were 51bp, nonperforming assets fell 1.6% q/q, and CET1 was a stable 10.8%.
The 10-Q baseline for Q2 2026: revenue $7.71B (+10.1% y/y), diluted EPS $1.35 (+21.6%), net income +19.9%. Q2 was the last filing-level read before the Q3 raise.

On the Q3 call management raised FY2026 guidance: net revenue growth of 8-9% (6-7% ex-BTIG) and about 300bp of operating leverage (about 400bp ex-BTIG), up from 200bp/300bp. For Q4 it guided NII +6-7% y/y (FTE), fees +13-14% (about half from BTIG), expenses about +8% (about +4% ex-BTIG), and NIM up by about the same 5bp as in Q3. A press report on Oct 24 repeats the Q4 guide.

The consensus growth rates in the fact sheet (+11.3% revenue, +16.5% EPS) use Q3 2025 ($7.33B / $1.22) as the 'year-ago' base. Backing Q4 2025 out of the filings gives about $7.36B of revenue and about $1.26 of EPS. On those bases, consensus of $8.16B / $1.42 is about +10.8% revenue and about +12.7% EPS. This is derived, not reported; Q4 2025 was not read directly.

The Q4 guide is NII (FTE) +6-7% y/y, fee revenue +13-14% (about half from BTIG) and noninterest expense about +8% (about +4% ex-BTIG). FY revenue growth guidance of 8-9% on FY2025 revenue of $28.66B, against $15.00B in H1 2026 and a Q3 of roughly $8.0B (about $7.97B, from $7.33B +8.7%), implies Q4 revenue of roughly $7.95-8.27B depending on exact Q3. The $8.16B consensus therefore sits in the upper half of that range. The dollar range rests on my reconstruction of Q3.

Consensus for Q4 is EPS of $1.42 on revenue of $8.16B. Q3 EPS was $1.34, including an impact of about $0.07 from reserve build. The sources give no Q4 provision, tax-rate or share-count guidance, so I do not derive a consensus-implied provision or my own EPS cases from them.

Capital: CET1 was 10.8% (stable) and AOCI-adjusted CET1 fell 30bp to 9.1% on $12B of RWA growth plus about 40bp from higher Treasury rates and wider spreads. TCE was 6.6%. Management paused buybacks in Q3 and expects to restart 'over the next quarter or two' toward a 70-75% payout, without relying on any Basel III endgame benefit.

On Oct 30 USB closed an issuance of Series P fixed-rate reset preferred stock: 1,000,000 depositary shares, each 1/25 of a $25,000-liquidation-preference share, so about $1B of gross Tier 1 (not CET1) capital. The filing does not state the use of proceeds.

view.text: Consensus is $1.42, against Q3 EPS of $1.34, which carried about $0.07 of reserve-build impact (EPS +10% y/y, or +16% excluding the build). Provision is the swing factor. Management gave no Q4 provision guidance, so a quantified EPS sensitivity cannot be built from the sources.

last_reported.text: Q3 NIM was 2.84%, up 5bp q/q (Q2: 2.79%; Q2 2025: 2.66%). NII (FTE) grew 5.6% y/y and 2.3% q/q.

view.text: Guide is NIM up a similar amount to Q3's +5bp, about 2.89%, and NII +6-7% y/y on an FTE basis. Supports: about $10B per quarter of fixed assets repricing at about +125bp, floating-rate loans at 30% of earning assets, and a full quarter of the Amazon card book. Fed funds futures pointed to a hold on Oct 28 and a hike in December, which leaves Q4 lightly exposed; the roughly 50% beta assumption is mostly a 2027 issue. Caution: the Q2 10-Q sensitivity table shows +200bp NII at only +0.29% (vs +0.80% at year-end) and +0.49% for -50bp, so the model view is not clearly asset-sensitive yet.

metrics_to_model.metric: Total fee revenue and capital markets

last_reported.text: Q3 fees +14.9% y/y; capital markets +69% (BTIG contributed $226M; legacy +10%). Fees were 44% of revenue.

view.text: Guide is +13-14% y/y with about half from BTIG (about $200M/quarter). Sequentially fees should dip because Q3 'other' had unusual gains (normal $120-150M), mortgage is hurt by higher rates, and merchant is about flat. Corporate payments (+19% in Q3), trust and card are the offsets. At BAC, Q3 investment banking fees were about -11% and market making about -26% y/y, while WFC's FICC trading fell. That is a read-across risk to the double-digit legacy capital markets growth and the BTIG run-rate.

metrics_to_model.metric: Noninterest expense, operating leverage and efficiency ratio

last_reported.text: Q3 expenses rose 7.1% y/y (2.0% ex-BTIG), with operating leverage of 240bp (440bp ex-BTIG). Efficiency ratio was just under 56% (Q2: 57.1%).

view.text: Guide is noninterest expense about +8% y/y (about +4% ex-BTIG). Full-year operating leverage guidance was raised to about 300bp (about 400bp ex-BTIG) from 200/300bp. Q3 expense grew 7.1% (2.0% ex-BTIG), with 440bp of operating leverage ex-BTIG. Consensus revenue of $8.16B is +11.3% y/y, about 3 points above the guided expense growth. Management put efficiency at around 56% and wants to move toward the middle of its mid-to-high 50s range.

metrics_to_model.metric: Provision for credit losses, net charge-offs and reserve

last_reported.text: Q3 NCOs were 51bp (Q2: 0.53%) and NPAs fell 1.6% q/q. Q3 EPS carried about $0.07 of reserve build. Allowance ratio was 1.94% at Q2.

view.text: No provision guidance exists. Q3's build looks tied to loan growth and the Amazon small-business card book ($1.7B period-end), which is my inference, not disclosed. Peers did not build broadly: BAC's allowance fell on card and CRE improvement, and WFC's rose only $121M YTD. I model a provision of about $0.55-0.70B. A larger build would be the largest downside to $1.42, and CRE and C&I/NDFI are the watch items as rates rise.

view.text: Expect CET1 around 10.8-11.0% if loan growth continues at about 1% per quarter. A restart announcement, or confirmation of timing, is the main capital swing for the print. Management ties timing to loan demand/RWA, rates and incoming rules. BAC kept repurchasing $6.0B in Q3, so USB's pause is a relative negative. Series P preferred adds Tier 1, not CET1.

since_filing.text: Q3 results and a guidance raise: record revenue of about $8B, EPS $1.34, and full-year revenue growth lifted to 8-9% and operating leverage to about 300bp. This is the key change from the Aug 6 10-Q, which preceded the BTIG contribution (closed June 1) and the Amazon small-business card portfolio.

BTIG contributed $226M of fee revenue in Q3 and is expected at about $200M per quarter. The Amazon small-business card portfolio added about $900M to average loans and $1.7B to period-end loans in Q3. Together they are over $1B of annual revenue onboarded.

Buybacks were paused in Q3 after strong loan growth, the Amazon book and the rate move. The 10-Q showed $3.912B left on the authorization at 6/30, with Q2 repurchases of about $200M. Peer BAC repurchased $6.0B in Q3 and issued $2.0B of preferred on Oct 23. USB's own Series P preferred closed Oct 30.

Rates moved against the bond portfolio and capital: management cited a September Fed hike, higher Treasury yields and wider spreads. Pre-meeting coverage on Oct 28 expected a hold with about 7% odds of an October hike, and a hike in December. The actual Oct 28 decision is not confirmed in the sources.

Peer Q3 filings read favorably for USB credit but mixed for capital markets. BAC's allowance fell on card and CRE improvement; WFC's rose only $121M YTD with auto and C&I charge-offs up. BAC investment banking fees fell about 11% y/y and market making about 26%; WFC trading fell on FICC. BAC's investment and brokerage fees rose about 14%, supportive of USB trust fees.

Regulatory timeline: management expects rule changes in Q4 and calls tailoring speculation; it is 'fully ready' to move to Category II regardless of Basel III endgame timing and cited about a 5% RWA benefit from the Basel proposal.

key_debates.question: Will provision normalize in Q4, making $1.42 beatable, or is credit cost the hidden risk to the consensus?

bull.text: Q3's reserve build cost about $0.07 of EPS, but credit metrics were healthy: net charge-offs fell 2bp to 51bp, nonperforming assets fell 1.6% linked-quarter, and management sees nothing on the consumer side. If the build does not repeat, EPS would have upside versus the $1.42 consensus.

bear.text: Q3 already carried a reserve build worth about $0.07 of EPS, and management gave no provision guidance. Higher rates are a watch item for CRE, and C&I charge-offs are higher at WFC and BAC.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 provision and reserve build disclosure, the allowance ratio versus 1.94% at Q2, and any commentary on the Amazon day-one reserve and the economic forecast.

key_debates.question: Is the NIM path to 2.90% in Q4 and 3% in 2027 robust to rate hikes and deposit competition?

bull.text: About $10B per quarter of fixed assets reprices about 125bp higher, floating-rate loans are 30% of earning assets, funding costs rose just 1bp in Q3 and consumer deposits hit a record. With the Fed expected to hold in October, Q4 deposit repricing is mostly known.

bear.text: The Q2 10-Q shows NII +0.29% for +200bp (vs +0.80% at year-end) and +0.49% for -50bp, so the balance sheet was not clearly asset-sensitive. An analyst asked about initial liability sensitivity at the short end. Beta could exceed the assumed 50% if hikes continue quarterly through mid-2027.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 NIM versus about 2.89-2.90%, the deposit cost trend, the December Fed decision, and the Q3 10-Q rate-sensitivity table.

key_debates.question: Can capital markets (BTIG plus legacy) sustain double-digit growth and a roughly $200M BTIG run-rate into Q4?

bull.text: Legacy capital markets grew 10% in Q3, led by commodities, FX and impact finance. Management expects strong growth next quarter, with legacy capital markets helping deliver double-digit y/y growth. BTIG is expected at about $200M, versus $226M in Q3.

bear.text: Peers show softness: BAC investment banking fees about -11% and market making about -26% y/y in Q3, and WFC FICC trading down. Half of Q4's guided fee growth comes from BTIG, so a miss hits the 13-14% guide directly, and capital markets is a high-efficiency-ratio business.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 capital markets revenue ex-BTIG growth, BTIG revenue versus about $200M, and the fall conference disclosure on capital markets.

key_debates.question: Do buybacks restart, and does Category II/AOCI treatment constrain capital return?

bull.text: USB generated 33bp of capital after dividends in Q3, CET1 held 10.8%, TCE held 6.6%, and management is 'committed to the 70-75% payout' and expects to restart within one or two quarters regardless of Basel relief.

bear.text: AOCI-adjusted CET1 fell to 9.1% on $12B of RWA growth and the rate backup. H1 distributions were only about 53% of income to common versus the 70-75% target. My estimate is that four-quarter average assets could reach $700B around Q4 2026 to Q1 2027, triggering Category II with AOCI in capital, full LCR/NSFR and annual stress tests.

key_debates.what_settles_it: A restart announcement or timing at the Q4 report, Q4 RWA growth, the 10-year yield, and final Basel/tailoring rules.

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: Revenue of about $8.2B (upper end of the guided range), expenses at or below $4.54B, and provision normalizing toward $0.55B give EPS of about $1.50-1.54, a clear beat. NIM prints about 2.90%, legacy capital markets stays in double digits, and management confirms a buyback restart. This is my scenario, not a forecast.

triggers: Q4 provision at or below about $0.55B, with no new reserve build
Revenue at or above about $8.15B and the efficiency ratio below 56%
Buyback restart timing confirmed or announced
NIM at or above 2.90% and 2027 NIM path toward 3% reiterated

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Revenue of about $8.0B, expenses of about $4.60B and provision of $0.70B or more give EPS of about $1.31, a miss. Capital markets and mortgage soften with higher rates, deposit costs outrun the 50% beta assumption, and a further reserve build or slower buyback restart weighs on the shares.

triggers: Provision above about $0.70B or a further reserve build
Legacy capital markets growth below 10% or BTIG well below $200M
NIM expansion below the guided 5bp or deposit beta above 50%
Buyback restart pushed beyond Q1 2027 or Category II timing accelerates

claim.text: Credit cost: higher rates could pressure CRE (office was 8.8% of CRE at year-end). Q3 already included a reserve build worth about $0.07 of EPS. Management says it is watching CRE as rates rise but sees nothing to call out yet.

Capital markets and BTIG: about half of guided Q4 fee growth is BTIG, and peers show weak market making and investment banking (BAC about -26% and -11% y/y). Management's own point is that capital markets is a high-efficiency-ratio business, which could push efficiency toward the high end of its mid-to-high 50s range.

Rates and deposit competition: a September Fed hike has been followed by expected further hikes (December widely expected). Deposit costs rose 7bp in Q3, management assumes a 50% beta, and the Q2 10-Q shows only a small positive NII sensitivity to +200bp.

Capital and regulatory: AOCI-adjusted CET1 is 9.1% and RWA grew $12B in one quarter. The buyback is paused, with resumption expected over the next quarter or two. A Category II transition would bring full LCR/NSFR and AOCI recognition in capital. Management expects rule changes in Q4, and final capital rules and tailoring are unconfirmed.

Integration and strategy risk: BTIG closed June 1 and the Amazon small-business card portfolio was onboarded in Q3. The 10-Q flags that BTIG benefits may take longer than expected and costs may be higher. BTIG adds market risk (included in Market Risk Rule capital from Q3 2026).

Mortgage and card fee drag: management expects limited y/y mortgage growth on higher rates, merchant revenue near 0% for the next couple of quarters, and other revenue normalizing to $120-150M after unusual Q3 gains. Q4 fee growth guidance of 13-14% is slightly below Q3's 14.9%.

Litigation: a Visa interchange injunctive settlement received preliminary approval in June 2026 with a final approval hearing set for November 16, 2026. The 10-Q says the Company's Visa swap obligation (derivative liability $74M at 6/30) is linked to the litigation, and also notes OCC fair-access inquiries.

questions_for_management.question: What was the Q3 provision and the split of the $0.07 reserve build between Amazon, loan growth and the macro forecast, and what provision should we assume for Q4?

why.text: Consensus Q4 EPS is $1.42, and the call gave no provision guidance. Q3 EPS was held to +10% y/y versus +16% excluding the reserve build.

questions_for_management.question: What specific conditions (RWA growth, 10-year yield, rules) trigger a buyback restart, and what pace of repurchases do you assume as you glide to the 70-75% payout?

why.text: Management said it expects to resume within a quarter or two and cited loan demand, rates and regulation, while $3.9B remained on the authorization at 6/30. Peer BAC kept buying back $6.0B in Q3.

questions_for_management.question: When do you expect to cross the $700B four-quarter average asset threshold for Category II, and what is the effective date and phase-in for AOCI?

why.text: Category II brings full LCR/NSFR and AOCI recognition in regulatory capital. Management says it is 'fully ready' regardless of the timing of Basel III endgame and gave no date; the AOCI-adjusted CET1 was 9.1% at Q3.

questions_for_management.question: How is BTIG tracking versus the $200M quarterly revenue assumption, what is its Q4 expense contribution, and what is the legacy capital markets growth outlook if fixed income softens?

why.text: About half of guided Q4 fee growth and a large part of the expense gap versus the ex-BTIG 4% comes from BTIG, and peers show weak market making.

questions_for_management.question: What deposit beta and cost assumptions underlie 2.90% NIM in Q4, and how do they change if the Fed hikes quarterly through mid-2027? Why does the 10-Q sensitivity show only +0.29% NII for +200bp?

why.text: The 10-Q shows a modest rate sensitivity while management describes a shift to asset sensitivity and assumes a roughly 50% beta.

questions_for_management.question: What are the 2027 operating leverage drivers, the expected efficiency ratio, and the branch and marketing investment plan, given Q4 is the thinnest operating leverage quarter?

why.text: Management guided positive operating leverage in 2027 on similar drivers but gave no numbers. Marketing was up 34% in Q2 and branch investment is rising to about $300M.

Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 NII, fee and expense bases are reconstructed from FY2025 less H1 less Q3, not read from filings; Q4 dollar bridges could shift by tens of millions.
No provision, tax-rate or reserve-build guidance for Q4 was located; the share count assumes no Q4 buyback.
The actual Oct 28 FOMC decision was not retrieved; a hold is inferred from pre-meeting expectations (about 7% odds of a hike). No fresh December hike odds were found.

No consensus for provision, NIM, fees or expense; no analyst 2027 operating leverage estimates; beat/miss record, price targets, whisper EPS and options-implied move were not available. The report date of Jan 19, 2027 is not confirmed.

Peer commentary from JPM, Citi and Goldman (Fortune, Oct 13) and PNC's Q3 release (Oct 15) are older than 14 days and were treated as background only; JPM and Citi investment banking and trading dollar figures were not found. WFC capital and buyback data were not retrieved.
No news within the last 14 days on final Basel III endgame, SCB averaging, or Fed reindexing of Category II/III thresholds; the Category II timing estimate uses assumed Q3/Q4 average assets.
How the company defines operating leverage (securities losses, notable items) is not confirmed; Q3 reported 240bp versus about 160bp from the simple revenue-minus-expense growth gap.

XBRL fields for operating income, capital expenditure and long-term debt are missing from the fact sheet (not meaningful for a bank); the Q3 10-Q (rate sensitivity, allowance ratio, remaining buyback authorization, RWA) was not yet available.
